reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected GAAP exhibit rows shows a materially different revenue mix and a much higher GAAP profit subtotal in the later quarter, with total operating expenses lower on a displayed basis. The revenue increase is concentrated in the license line while the recurring SaaS/PaaS line declined sequentially, so the mix shift argues against reading the quarter as broad-based recurring-demand strength. The profit improvement is a GAAP subtotal comparison only; the selected rows contain no segment, margin, backlog, bookings, deferred-revenue, non-GAAP, or guidance data, and no source reconciliation linking any driver to the profit change. Income tax expense rose in the same direction as pretax income, so the tax line is not evidence of a smaller tax drag. Because the selected evidence cannot separate timing-driven license recognition from a durable change in recurring demand, and cannot establish a causal driver for the profit move, the research state is held for review rather than upgraded or invalidated.
